headword: {卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}
reading: そつぎょうしょうしょ

definitions.explanation: The official document presented to a student at graduation, certifying completion of a course of study. Traditionally handed out one by one at the graduation ceremony.

examples.japanese: {卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}を{受|う}け{取|と}った。
{校長先生|こうちょうせんせい}から{卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}を{授与|じゅよ}された。
examples.english: I was presented with my diploma by the principal.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}な{卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}を{筒|つつ}に{入|い}れて{保管|ほかん}している。
examples.english: I keep my precious diploma stored in a tube.

notes:
Composed of {卒業|そつぎょう} (graduation) + {証書|しょうしょ} (certificate). At Japanese graduation ceremonies, the diploma is traditionally handed out individually with a brief bow, often rolled into a cardboard tube for transport home.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}を{受|う}け{取|と}る: to receive a diploma
- {卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}を{授与|じゅよ}する: to present a diploma
- {卒業証書|そつぎょうしょうしょ}{授与式|じゅよしき}: diploma presentation ceremony

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {修了証書|しゅうりょうしょうしょ}: completion certificate — for finishing a course or program that isn't a full degree
- {学位記|がくいき}: degree certificate — specifically a university degree certificate, more formal
